name: Brut
prior: Interactive-evolution synths are a known, playable family: Sonic Charge Synplant (2008) / Synplant 2 (2023) - a seed at the centre, branches toward notes that mutate the sound more the further they grow, a DNA double-helix editor, 'capture evolved DNA as a new seed', Genopatch seeds from audio (VS: musicradar.com synplant-2 review, soniccharge.com/synplant, synthanatomy.com 2023/10, synthtopia.com 2023/10/04); MendelSynth (iPhone) - simulated genomes, double-tap = six mutated children around the parent, drag = cross two parents, mutation-rate control (VS: synthtopia.com/?p=24940); Dillon Bastan 'Natural Selection S' (M4L) - preset values as DNA mixed and mutated over generations, user selects (VS: isotonikstudios.com natural-selection-s); Nord Modular G2 'Patch Mutator' (editor 1.4, Dahlstedt) - interactive evolution of patch parameters, mating variations (VS: nordkeyboards.com G2 Mutator manual, electro-music.com post-41805), from 'A MutaSynth in Parameter Space' 2001 (VS: research.chalmers.se 59129); Synapse Dune 3.5 'Genetics' (VS: comment on synthanatomy, unverified). Academic: ESSynth evolutionary waveform populations (VS: researchgate 51999706), 'Directed Evolution in Live Coding' (VS: zenodo 4285412), Smith 'Play it again' evolved patches (VS: scholarworks.iupui.edu 1805/14980), GP synth (VS: code.soundsoftware.ac.uk/projects/gpsynth). In Myzel: dice(). Not found: an instrument in which the played note itself is the selection step - each note a child of the pool, hold time x pressure as fitness, Puls lanes breeding their own line; the two extended searches returned nothing for per-note inheritance or hold time as fitness.
costNotes: The synthesis (6 inharmonic partials with own decay and sustain, formant bandpass, breath band) does not need sample-level DSP: natively 6 sine oscillators + 6 gains (0.36) + formant biquad (0.1) + noise + breath biquad (0.1) + mix (0.06) = about 0.5-0.6 units, the same model Schale uses (sch = 0.9 with its periodic-wave trick, APP 3732); per-partial envelopes are setTargetAtTime on each gain, Bebung/Gestik via v.mod on every oscillator detune, setF glides all six. Worklet version: node 0.06 + 3 params 0.09 + 6 complex-rotation partials about 0.2 (16 = 0.6 measured) + formant and breath as two more resonators 0.03 + exciter 0.05 = 0.45 (R: webaudio.md section 4); the idea's 0.25 for a 'JS 2-pole bandpass' assumes a biquad at 36 ns/sample - as a rotation it is 5 ns. L3: 12 partials native 0.95, worklet 0.7. Recommendation: native first; worklet only if sample-accurate per-partial envelopes or 12+ partials matter. Genome logistics (pool, fitness integral, parent choice) are main-thread per note, free. Simulation (sim/bio2_sim.py): with sigma = 0.3 x 0.3 = 0.09 ln per note on a log gene, a pure clamped random walk keeps the median near the Urahn but the 10-90 % band of rho_2 is 2.1-3.7 after 20 notes, 1.5-5.2 after 100, 1.4-7.5 after 1000 with 10 % of lines pinned at the clamps; a mean-reversion term theta = 0.05-0.15 toward the Urahn holds the band at 1.9-3.9 / 2.2-3.5 for ever. Breeding is felt: a player who holds notes near rho_2 = 2 ten times longer pulls the running median within 10 % of the target after a median of 23 notes (90 % within 47) at Auslese exponent 1, 17/28 at exponent 4.
soundHeld: A held Brut note is a decaying inharmonic cluster that settles onto its sustain partials with a formant and breath - Schale/Glocke territory with a vowel; Hoehe = 'Nahrung' tilting partials, formant and sustain is a reasonable live timbre control, Bebung on the detune bus is trivial. The distinctive part is not audible in one note: it is the drift between notes. Over 20 notes the ratios have wandered by a factor ~1.4 (sim), which is clearly audible as 'the instrument is changing', and the breeding loop (hold what you like) converges within ~20-50 notes, fast enough to be felt in a minute of play. Identity risk is real: the engine's fixed signature must sit in the exciter (impulse + Biss noise) and the formant, or presets just sound like a slightly detuned Schale.
soundBurst: A Puls hit is a short-lived child: impulse + Biss noise into six decaying partials under burstEnv - a good mallet/bowl hit, inharmonic and vowel-coloured, tempo-robust. Risks: a lane at 8 hits/s mutates its own line 8x faster than fingers and, with 'small fitness' children still entering the pool, pollutes the finger lineage; keep lane children out of the shared pool (or scale sigma by 1/sqrt(rate)) so the lane varies around the current pool instead of running away. Without mean reversion, an hour-long lane (3600 notes) random-walks into the clamps.
failureModes: Genome random walk: without a reversion term toward the Urahn the timbre degenerates to the gene bounds within ~1000 notes (Puls lanes get there in minutes)
Identity: one note sounds like a Schale/Glocke variant; the evolution is only audible across notes - needs a fixed exciter signature, the formant, and the 'Generation N' display
Presets not reproducible (pool state); save the lineage (pool genomes + generation) in the preset or declare it a living preset
Polyphony: chords of siblings with different genomes beat and smear; sweet for pads, mush for harmony - option 'Geschwister gleich' (one genome per chord)
Puls lanes breed too fast and pollute the finger pool; lane children should not enter the pool
Worklet route would move the whole graph to the worklet thread for a sound that needs no worklet (R: webaudio.md section 2) - build natively
Fitness = hold x pressure rewards drones: a player holding a chord for a minute floods the pool with one genome (pool <= 6) - cap fitness at ~8 s
verdict: Rare: interactive evolution is a known playable family - Synplant 2's seed/branches and DNA, MendelSynth's tap-to-breed, Nord G2's Patch Mutator, Natural Selection S - but none makes the played note the selection step with hold time as fitness; that mechanic was not found in two extended searches. It is native-feasible at about 0.5 units (six sines, formant, breath; a worklet buys nothing here), and the simulation says the loop works: a preference is bred in within ~20-50 notes, while an unselected lane random-walks the genome to its clamps within ~1000 notes unless a mean-reversion term (theta 0.05-0.15) is added and lane children stay out of the pool. Held and Puls notes are musically solid but timbrally ordinary (inharmonic partials plus vowel = Schale territory), so Brut's identity must be carried by a fixed exciter signature, the formant and the generation display, and presets need the lineage saved.
